relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-backup-service-nodes-threads-map
relations.evidence: This will overwrite the map in the backup service with the number of threads allocated to the backup service node with UUID `23ec390488495fec2074119a61d2eb91` to 3.

relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-backup-service-nodes-threads-map
relations.evidence: This will add a new entry to the backup service's nodes threads map, allocating 4 threads to the backup service node with UUID `76dc6557ed98ac7e78e70cf0d28921f3`.

notable_absence.finding: No RBAC role stated for --set/--add, which overwrite or extend a cluster-wide per-node resource allocation. Separately, a genuine terminology drift within the page itself: the page's own title and H1 are 'backup-service-nodes-threads-map' (with '-map'), but the SYNOPSIS token and every EXAMPLES invocation use 'nodes-threads' (without '-map') as the literal sub-subcommand name - 'nodes-threads --get', 'nodes-threads --set ...', 'nodes-threads --add ...'. A reader following the page title literally would type the wrong command. This is a textbook symptom of the round's authorship-provenance hypothesis: a docs filename/title drifting from the actual CLI token, uncaught by review.

cross_component_finding: Confirms backup:nodes-threads-map-endpoint's registry note that this setting is 'REST-surface-only, NO cbbackupmgr CLI equivalent' in the sense that cbbackupmgr indeed has nothing like it - but this page shows couchbase-cli (the OTHER CLI) does wrap it, via backup-service nodes-threads. So 'no CLI equivalent' should be read as 'no cbbackupmgr equivalent' specifically; couchbase-cli's wrapper is a thin pass-through with no additional semantics beyond the REST fields (node UUID, thread count) - it does not, for instance, expose the CPU-core-based default formula that the REST/conceptual pages describe.
